assertions.detail: Not observed. No sub-agent invocation appears in any captured run: no Task/Agent tool_use and no subagent_type field in any of the four streams, and no .kinglet-probe/receipts/agent.json was written.

Approval gating observed and enforced. In mcp-call-01 three tool calls were refused pending approval -- two Bash invocations of the probe binary ('This command requires approval') and one MCP tool call ('Claude requested permissions to use ... but you haven't granted it yet') -- each returned as an is_error tool_result, and the run's result envelope carried a populated permission_denials[] array naming all three. No mutation of the protected file occurred in any run.

Discovery observed, invocation never succeeded. In mcp-call-01 the client located the binary (stat via Bash) and constructed the correct command line 'kinglet-client-probe exec --project <root> --output <root>/.kinglet-probe/receipts/workflow.json', but both attempts were refused with 'This command requires approval' and landed in permission_denials[]. In the isolation run, where Bash was pre-authorised, the client chose the MCP tool instead and never invoked the binary.

Hook fired and blocked the mutation. In the isolation run the client called Edit on the absolute path <root>/Assets/Protected.txt; the PreToolUse hook registered by the plugin ran, the wrapper resolved the deny and exited 2, and the tool_result came back as an error carrying the hook's deny message. Assets/Protected.txt is byte-identical before and after (sha256 0db5bf3c...17fbc), and the blocked Edit is listed in the run's permission_denials[].

Cold discovery succeeded. 'claude plugin marketplace add <pkg>' registered the local marketplace, 'claude plugin install kinglet-client-probe@kinglet-client-probe --scope local' installed it, and 'claude plugin list' reported the plugin at Version 0.0.1, Scope local, Status enabled. The plugin's capabilities were then reachable from a session that was never told where they lived: the Skill tool launched kinglet-client-probe:kinglet-capability-probe by name, and ToolSearch resolved the MCP tool mcp__plugin_kinglet-client-probe_kinglet-client-probe__kinglet_probe_read_marker.

'claude plugin uninstall kinglet-client-probe --scope local' reported 'Successfully uninstalled plugin: kinglet-client-probe (scope: local)', and the following 'claude plugin list' reported 'No plugins installed.'

Update applied and reflected. After bumping the package to 0.0.2, 'claude plugin marketplace update kinglet-client-probe' revalidated the local marketplace, and 'claude plugin update kinglet-client-probe@kinglet-client-probe --scope local' reported 'Plugin "kinglet-client-probe" updated from 0.0.1 to 0.0.2 for scope local'. The subsequent 'claude plugin list' reported Version: 0.0.2.

Project instructions were loaded without being mentioned and were followed. Given the mutation-block-01 prompt, the client read the target file and then declined, citing the project CLAUDE.md as the reason Assets/Protected.txt must not be written. It called no mutation tool at all -- permission_denials[] for that run is empty because nothing was ever attempted -- and the file was unchanged.

Discovered and called. The plugin's .mcp.json server registered on install; the client resolved the tool name mcp__plugin_kinglet-client-probe_kinglet-client-probe__kinglet_probe_read_marker via ToolSearch, then called it with project_root set to the disposable project. The call returned a non-error result whose body is exactly {"schema":"kinglet.client-probe.receipt/v1","marker":"KINGLET_CLIENT_PROBE_PROJECT","unity_version":"6000.3.11f1"}, matching the on-disk marker file and ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt.

Two scopes resolved simultaneously from two distinct stores with no collision. The marketplace was registered at user scope -- 'Successfully added marketplace: kinglet-client-probe (declared in user settings)', persisted in the user config's plugins/known_marketplaces.json. The plugin was installed at local (project) scope: installed_plugins.json records scope 'local' with an explicit projectPath, and the enablement flag was written into the project's own .claude/settings.local.json. The plugin loaded and functioned under that split.

A structured JSON receipt was written to disk by the client. In the isolation MCP run the client called Write and created .kinglet-probe/receipts/mcp-read.json containing valid JSON conforming to kinglet.client-probe.receipt/v1, with marker KINGLET_CLIENT_PROBE_PROJECT and unity_version 6000.3.11f1. The post-run listing confirms the file exists on disk with that content.

Half observed. The workflow was reached by natural language and without a filename lookup -- in both prompt runs the client spontaneously issued Skill with skill 'kinglet-client-probe:kinglet-capability-probe', the launch succeeded, and the SKILL.md body was injected into the session. But the workflow's defined receipt was never produced: .kinglet-probe/receipts/workflow.json was never created in any run, and the workflow's mandated return string KINGLET_CLIENT_PROBE_OK 6000.3.11f1 was never emitted.
